# Den Lennie Field Guides

> Straight answers on pricing, scope, positioning and growth for video production business owners. Den Lennie is an author and business coach for video production company owners, with three decades in production, more than a decade running his own production company, and eight years coaching owners through VBA (Video Business Accelerator). These field guides hold the questions video business owners actually ask, answered plainly.

## About

- [About Den Lennie](https://docs.denlennie.com/about-den-lennie): Author and coach for video business owners. Three decades in production, five books including The S.C.A.L.E. Method (2026), and VBA clients generating more than $52M in additional revenue over eight years.
- [What VBA offers](https://docs.denlennie.com/vba-services): Coaching, community and tools for video production company owners. One programme, the VBA Elite Boardroom, plus the VBA AI toolset built for video production companies.
- [What VBA members say](https://docs.denlennie.com/vba-results): Results and testimonials from video business owners. $52M+ in additional revenue across members over eight years, in their own words.

## The S.C.A.L.E. Method and books

- [What is the S.C.A.L.E. Method?](https://docs.denlennie.com/scale-method): The framework from Den's 2026 book. Five disciplines a video business grows through: Survival, Control, Alignment, Leverage, Expansion.
- [The books Den Lennie has written](https://docs.denlennie.com/den-lennie-books): Five books for video business owners over more than a decade, including The S.C.A.L.E. Method (2026) and Business for Filmmakers (2014).

## Case studies

- [How a missing boundary cost a video business a client](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-revision-rounds): A video edit that blew past its agreed revision rounds and ended in a client walkout. Anonymised.
- [How a video business owner stopped guessing on every quote](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-pricing-system): A hundred quotes in and still freezing on every one, until a real pricing method ended the anxiety. Anonymised.
- [How a video business owner started moving off the project treadmill](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-recurring-revenue): Pricing a one-off filming day, then building a cost-of-delivery model and testing recurring packages. Anonymised.

## Pricing

- [What it costs to work with Den Lennie and VBA](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-guide): One programme, one price. The VBA Elite Boardroom is $1,700 USD a month, flat, cancel anytime. No onboarding fee, no minimum term, no application. Earlier programmes (Ascend, the Growth Strategy Session) are closed to new members.
- [How to price a video project so every quote isn't a guess](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-system): Day rate in four steps, the four-section quote, the ballpark script and what to say when a client pushes back, with a worksheet, quote skeleton and worked example to copy. Downloadable PDF.
- [Pricing Calculator: your day rate and a quote that holds](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-calculator): Floor and day rate from real overheads and sellable days, then a four-section quote with fee and contingency. Free, runs in the browser.
- [Charging for the invisible work: travel, delivery, storage, extras](https://docs.denlennie.com/charging-for-invisible-work): Travel, delivery, storage, extras: the work a video client never sees is the work owners give away for free. The four lines that belong on every quote, with the exact invoice wording: travel beyond 60 minutes each way, raw footage delivery, 12-month storage, and the extra half day on site. Plus the included-and-extra paragraph, a worked example and the rule. Downloadable PDF.
- [How many revision rounds to include, and how to charge for extra ones](https://docs.denlennie.com/revision-rounds): Two rounds of revisions per deliverable holds only if you define a round on the quote, count the rounds out loud at every delivery, and offer a choice before round three starts. The revision clause, a round definition, the scoreboard line, the pushback script, the price of an extra round and a worked example, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [The three revision emails, including the one for round three](https://docs.denlennie.com/revisions-field-guide): Three client email templates for revision rounds, led by the one to send when a client asks for changes after round two, plus what goes in the quote so they hold.
- [When a client's budget is lower than your quote, drop the scope, not the price](https://docs.denlennie.com/drop-scope-not-price): What to do when a client's budget is lower than your video quote: hold the rate, keep planning and filming, take deliverables and rounds out, and say it as a trade. The scope script, a three-option scope-down, the inclusions and exclusions wording, and a worked example, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [Why knowing your numbers lets you price with confidence](https://docs.denlennie.com/know-your-numbers): The three numbers every video business owner has to know: the floor a day must clear, the margin on each job built from crew at real day rates plus direct costs, and margin per day by client. A per-job margin worksheet, a monthly numbers review checklist, and the three-client example that shows why ranking clients by revenue gives the wrong answer. Downloadable PDF.
- [How much does my video business need to make, and can I deliver it?](https://docs.denlennie.com/what-the-business-needs-to-make): How to work out what your video business needs to make: cost the life you want, add what the business costs to run, then check the number against your packages times capacity, the revenue ceiling. Goal sheet, revenue sheet and monthly target tracker to copy into a spreadsheet, with worked examples. Downloadable PDF.
- [How do I get paid on time, and what terms should I set?](https://docs.denlennie.com/getting-paid-on-time): How to get paid on time for video work: put a deposit (Den Lennie normally insisted on 50 per cent up front) and the balance terms on the quote, ask accounts what a correct invoice needs, track every invoice on a forecast, chase on the dates, set the tax aside, and only discount in exchange for faster payment. Copy-and-paste terms, invoice line, reminders and a worked example. Downloadable PDF.

## Sales and clients

- [What to say when a prospect asks for a ballpark price](https://docs.denlennie.com/ballpark-price): What to say in the ten seconds after a prospect asks 'roughly how much?': give a range built the way you build a quote, make scope the variable, end with a question. The spoken script, the email reply, the line for 'can you just give me one number', and a worked example in round numbers. Downloadable PDF.
- [What to charge for video work: the pricing checklist](https://docs.denlennie.com/price-checklist): What to charge for video work, and the six checks to run before any price leaves your mouth or your outbox: cost of a delivered day, a range for a ballpark, specific numbers, the whole job priced, four quote sections with contingency and a production company fee, and scope that moves while the price holds. A copy-and-paste checklist, a before-you-send routine and a worked example. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to get paid for everything you deliver: the scope checklist](https://docs.denlennie.com/paid-checklist): Six checks that keep every piece of video work paid, a fill-in scope line for the quote (what's included, what's priced as an extra, what triggers a variation), and the script for the moment a client says "while you're here". All copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [The profitable quote checklist](https://docs.denlennie.com/quote-checklist): The pre-send checklist for a profitable video quote: three priced working sections, a 10 per cent contingency on the subtotal, a production company fee of 15 to 30 per cent on the production cost, inclusions stated, terms visible, one next step. Checklist, quote page skeleton and a worked example of a draft the checklist catches, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to qualify a video lead before you pitch](https://docs.denlennie.com/qualify-before-you-pitch): How to qualify a video lead before you quote: why sending the showreel and waiting loses, the five diagnostic questions for the first call, how to read fit, budget, decision-maker and timing, and a get-a-quote form with thank-you page wording. All copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to show real authority on a sales call](https://docs.denlennie.com/sales-call-authority): How to run a 30-minute discovery call with a video client: five questions that show authority, a summary back in their words, two or three options with their costs, and one dated next step. One-page call plan, summary-back line and options email, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to write a follow-up email that gets a reply](https://docs.denlennie.com/follow-up-emails): How to write a follow-up email that gets a reply and how many times to follow up: add one useful thing, end on the next step, and keep to a cadence. Three emails, a cadence for your calendar or CRM, and next-step closers, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to push back on a client without losing them](https://docs.denlennie.com/push-back-without-losing-client): How to push back on a video client without losing them: why absorbing the cost teaches the wrong lesson, a five-step way to draw a line calmly, and copy-and-paste replies for extra work, late payment, a moved deadline, a fee cut after delivery, and raw footage that wasn't agreed. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to get more from referrals and networking](https://docs.denlennie.com/follow-up-referrals): Why warm introductions and networking contacts go cold, and how to stop it: following up an introduction or event contact within days, and asking a happy client for a referral without it being awkward. Four messages to copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.

## Marketing

- [Content or outreach: where to spend your marketing time](https://docs.denlennie.com/content-vs-outreach): How to tell whether content or outreach is holding your video business back, then run a seven-day outreach test on one channel and read the result. Self-check, first-message template and test plan, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [The marketing asset you already have and keep ignoring](https://docs.denlennie.com/use-what-you-have): How to market a video business with work you've already delivered: audit your archive, then turn one finished job into a case study and a filmed client testimonial. Archive worksheet, case study structure, testimonial request email and interview questions, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [Feast or famine: why your video business swings, and the fix](https://docs.denlennie.com/feast-or-famine): Why video production work comes in waves and how to make it steady: a weekly marketing hour that doesn't move when the work lands, a message for the people you spoke to months ago, and the marketing Parthenon, built one lead source at a time. Calendar block, pillar audit and message, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How do I connect with the right people on LinkedIn without being a pest?](https://docs.denlennie.com/linkedin-connecting): How video business owners can connect with the right people on LinkedIn without being a pest: a profile checklist, the room check before you comment, a connection note to send after commenting, a first message with no pitch and one question, two follow-up notes, a weekly routine, and Den Lennie's own accept-rate test. Downloadable PDF.
- [How do I get my video business found on Google locally?](https://docs.denlennie.com/google-business-profile): How a video production business gets found on Google locally: set up the Google Business Profile with the right categories, services and description, link it to your website, post weekly and ask for reviews. Set-up checklist, category and service list, weekly posting template and review request, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.

## Positioning

- [How to choose a niche for your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/niche-paralysis): You don't have a lead problem, you have a 'who am I for' problem. How to find your niche in your last twelve months of jobs (margin, repeat, fit and proof), write it as a one-sentence niche-message-offer hypothesis, and test it with the people it describes before you touch your website. Job audit worksheet, hypothesis block and a test script, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to use your own story to position your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/your-story-positioning): Your background is usually your strongest positioning asset, and most owners walk straight past it.
- [How do I write the one line that says who I help?](https://docs.denlennie.com/message-equation): How to write the one line that says who your video business helps: the message equation (We help [niche] get [result] through [offer]), a homepage hero checklist, two anonymised homepages broken down, and a short script for testing the line with clients before it goes on the site. Downloadable PDF.
- [How do I find out why clients really hire me?](https://docs.denlennie.com/ask-framework): The ASK framework: three to five recorded fifteen-minute conversations with clients who already value you, five questions each, and their exact words sorted into triggers, frustrations, outcomes and feelings. The interview request email, the five questions, the referral ask and a worksheet, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to build a client avatar for a video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/client-avatar): A client avatar is one buyer described in enough detail to write every quote, email and web page to that person. The 13-step method, a worksheet to copy and fill in, five lines that answer a buyer's problem, and a worked example comparing two illustrative buyers. Downloadable PDF.

## Growth

- [How to move from one-off video projects to recurring revenue](https://docs.denlennie.com/recurring-revenue): One-off video work resets every month. How to turn a deliverable you already make into a monthly retainer: find the repeatable work, package it, price it in the house quote order, and propose it to an existing client. Retainer skeleton, the email, the line for "we don't need video every month", and a worked example in round numbers. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to grow revenue from the clients you already have](https://docs.denlennie.com/account-expansion): How to grow revenue from the clients you already have: rank them by margin per day rather than revenue, find the next project and the other departments or teams, then open the conversation with an end-of-project review email and an introduction request. Worksheet and emails, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [When one big client owns your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/one-client-dependency): How to measure and reduce dependence on one big client in a video business: a client concentration check with share of revenue, margin per day and a leave test, a profile of your best client to find more like them, the review conversation that protects the anchor, and a twelve-month plan in four quarters. Downloadable PDF.
- [What should I look at in my last twelve months before I change anything?](https://docs.denlennie.com/twelve-month-audit): Before you change your offer, marketing or niche, audit the last twelve months: where the revenue came from, what you kept, which clients cost the most time, what you're known for and how your last five clients describe you. Audit worksheet, client email and a one-page client sort, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.

All copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.

Annual list, quarterly priorities sheet, weekly five and quarterly review questions, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How do I get three real hours of work done a day?](https://docs.denlennie.com/three-real-hours): How a video business owner gets three hours of focused, goal-moving work out of a day: the CEO test, the four Ds, email twice a day with the touch-it-once rule, one list, and Schedule it Done (no more than three hours of above-the-line work a day, 30 minutes of white space). Four Ds sheet, email signature line, the three email options and a week template, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.

## Mindset

- [Handling the imposter feeling in your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/imposter-syndrome): How to handle the imposter feeling in a video business: tell a skills gap from a confidence gap, build an evidence file of projects, client words, repeat work, referrals and numbers, and read a short reframe before a big pitch. Self-check, evidence file template and pitch reframe, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [Getting your weekends back as a video business owner](https://docs.denlennie.com/weekends-back): How to get your weekends back as a video business owner: why more revenue never does it, how to write your version of success life first, book three non-negotiables into the diary before the work, and set the revenue goal last. Worksheet, diary list, quarterly review and Den Lennie's own vision boards as the worked example. Downloadable PDF.

## Choosing a coach
- [What a video business coach actually does](https://docs.denlennie.com/what-a-video-business-coach-does): What a video business coach works on (the seven systems every production company runs on), what happens week to week, what coaching doesn't do, and a one-page brief to send any coach before a first conversation. Downloadable PDF.
- [When a video production company is ready for a coach](https://docs.denlennie.com/when-ready-for-video-business-coach): The signs a video production company is ready for a coach, a readiness check to fill in, what too early looks like, why revenue alone doesn't decide it, and when to wait even past the baseline. Downloadable PDF.
- [Video business coach vs a generic business coach](https://docs.denlennie.com/video-business-coach-vs-generic): Hire a specialist video business coach when most of your problems come from how video gets quoted, made and delivered; a strong generalist when they don't. A sorting test for your problems, five questions to test any coach on video production, and a worked example. Downloadable PDF.
- [Coaching for videographers vs production company owners](https://docs.denlennie.com/coaching-videographers-vs-production-companies): A solo videographer usually needs focus and a production company owner usually needs structure, so the coaching differs. A ten-line self-check to find your first no, the question to ask any coach, and a worked example showing why revenue isn't the test. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to choose a coach for your video production company](https://docs.denlennie.com/how-to-choose-video-business-coach): How to choose a video business coach: start with your own constraint, compare coaches on five checks, and know what a first conversation should feel like. Includes three questions to answer before you speak to anyone and a side-by-side sheet to copy. Downloadable PDF.
- [Questions to ask a video business coach before you hire them](https://docs.denlennie.com/questions-to-ask-video-business-coach): The questions to send a video business coach before you sign up, what clear answers sound like, the questions a good coach should ask you, and how to check a claim yourself. Copy the full list into an email. Downloadable PDF.
- [What video business coaching costs](https://docs.denlennie.com/video-business-coaching-cost): The cost of a video business coach is the monthly fee times the minimum term, plus anything up front, plus your hours. An email asking any coach for the full cost, a year-one cost sheet, a worked comparison in round numbers, and what the VBA Elite Boardroom costs. Downloadable PDF.
- [Is a video business coach worth it](https://docs.denlennie.com/is-a-video-business-coach-worth-it): A video business coach is worth it when the cost of standing still, in your own numbers, is bigger than a year of fees and you'll do the work between calls. A cost-of-standing-still worksheet, a break-even bar per job, a worked example in round numbers, and who the Elite Boardroom isn't for. Downloadable PDF.
